## Unblinding

Compound: **cisplatin** (PubChem CID [5702198](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5702198))

ChEMBL mechanisms: DNA inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **DNA replication**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA damage**.

## Reflection

The initial Protein degradation call (p=0.58) overfit a pooled atlas comparison. That atlas actually favored Protein synthesis 4/10 over degradation 2/10 with tight similarities 0.61-0.68, but I weighted lactacystin/MG-132 neighbours and nonspecific enlargement (cell_area z=+10.5 at 10 uM) plus cell loss. The reviewer was right that the 30 uM well (nuc_form_factor z=-11.9, cell_count z=-11.6, act contrast z=+11.2) was qualitatively toxic and contaminated the signal.

Isolating the 10 uM-only atlas was correct and moved the call into the right neighborhood: DNA replication 6/10 versus DNA damage 1/10 and Aurora 2/10, with intact filaments arguing against Eg5/Aurora/microtubule MoAs. Cisplatin is a DNA inhibitor that produces cisplatin-damaged DNA (PMID 30990031) and strand breakage/crosslinking in MCF-7 cells (PMID 15294448), damage that normally engages repair (PMID 19887555).

The remaining miss was replication versus damage. With only two rep1 high-dose wells and no valid 3-well dose response, enlargement plus loss was nonspecific and I had no EdU versus gamma-H2AX functional split, so I over-weighted the 6/10 count and chose DNA replication 0.62 while leaving true DNA damage at 0.12.

What was right:
- Recognized 30 uM well as toxic/outlier with extreme nuclear irregularity and severe cell loss and excluded it on re-analysis, isolating the 10 uM driver signal.
- Correctly deprioritized Eg5/Aurora/microtubule MoAs because visual fields showed intact filamentous tubulin/actin without mitotic arrest despite enlargement.
- Moved from proteasome/synthesis to DNA-targeting space on 10 uM-only atlas and retained DNA damage as second hypothesis, placing final call adjacent to truth.

What was wrong or missed:
- First conclusion Protein degradation 0.58 overstated separation from pooled atlas that favored Protein synthesis 4/10 vs degradation 2/10 at 0.61-0.68 similarities.
- Final DNA replication over DNA damage relied on 6/10 vs 1/10 atlas counts without EdU, gamma-H2AX, or DNA-content data to distinguish replication arrest from damage response.
- Acquisition of only 10 uM and 30 uM rep1 left no replicate and no valid dose_response, making cell_area enlargement and cell_count loss nonspecific.

Proposed next experiment: Repeat cisplatin at 1-10 uM in triplicate with EdU incorporation plus gamma-H2AX and DNA-content flow cytometry, including floxuridine/methotrexate as replication controls and cisplatin/MMS as damage controls, to separate DNA replication arrest from DNA damage response.
